title: Predicting U.S. Power Outage Duration
description: Built a modeling pipeline on 1,500+ real-world outage records using feature engineering, permutation tests, and gradient boosting, improving prediction accuracy by 57%.
Wrote a stakeholder report with a fairness audit checking model robustness across subgroups.

title: Historical Redlining & Environmental Burden
description: Merged three real-world datasets and used OLS regression and Welch's t-test to link 1930s redlining grades to today's pollution burden (r = 0.63, p = 0.012, R² = 0.42).
Presented results to a non-technical audience in a written report and recorded briefing.

title: Support Ticket Memory Agent
description: LLM agent that answers support questions using memory of past solved tickets, built with Python, TF-IDF retrieval, and the Claude API.
Learns from user feedback and reached a 90% top-3 retrieval hit rate on reworded test questions.

title: Persuasive or Deceptive Visualization?
description: DSC 106 group project on the claim that the life expectancy gap between rich and poor countries has largely closed, using World Bank data (1960 to 2019).
Built one chart for and one against the claim, then rated each design choice from deceptive to earnest.

title: Casino Revenue Time Series Analysis
description: Reviewed a published study on whether poker rooms make money for Las Vegas casinos and found it mixed model selection with inference.
Ran a proper time series inference workflow in R, with sensitivity analyses.

title: Relative Risks, Odds Ratios, and Logistic Regression
description: Computed relative risks and odds ratios in R from a meat consumption and colon cancer study.
Explained why relative risk fails in case-control designs and fit a logistic regression with BMI.

title: Model Selection and Inference on MLB Salaries
description: Used simulation in R to show how dropping covariates based on p-values inflates the Type I error rate.
Applied a proper inference workflow and log transformations to model 1986/87 MLB player salaries.

title: Danceability and Spotify Popularity
description: COGS 9 group project asking if artists active from 2018 to 2025 with more danceable music are more popular on Spotify.
Used a Kaggle dataset of tracks from about 30,000 artists, with a research review and an ethics plan for bias and fair modeling.

title: Bias in Machine Learning
description: COGS 9 assignment using interactive simulations from "The Myth of the Impartial Machine."
Studied sampling error, dataset bias in ImageNet, how imbalanced data pushes models to amplify bias, and feedback loops.

title: Python Snake Game Workshop
description: Women in Computer Science workshop at Diablo Valley College with 20+ attendees.
Coded a Snake game in Python together, then played against each other.

title: Alma: UX/UI and Graphic Design
description: Graphic and UX/UI designer at an AI LegalTech startup making immigration easier ($5.1M raised).
Designed data-driven UI improvements for navigation and accessibility.
Analyzed 200+ survey responses to improve content clarity and user flow.

title: Fluent.ai: UX/UI Design
description: UX/UI designer for an English learning app for IT specialists, founded by a Stanford LdX graduate.
Interviewed 15+ IT professionals and prototyped the full app workflow in Figma.
Worked with engineers to align designs with backend functionality.
